g.id: Treated effluent sold: volume times price, capped by irrigation demand not by what we treat
STEP 3. Revenue and avoided cost, every year
Sewerage and connection charges, if NWS levies them
Avoided cost: tanker haulage, septic emptying, deferring the SUREKHA plant
Energy: pumping at the lifting stations, aeration at the plant
STEP 2. OPEX, built bottom-up, every year
Sludge handling and disposal, and chemicals
Labour, jetting, CCTV, desludging and odour control
Replacing mechanical and electrical plant inside the 25 years
Gravity sewers: rate per metre by diameter AND depth band
Manholes by depth, and house connections per property
Force mains and lifting stations: civil plus mechanical and electrical
STP at OMR per cubic metre per day, and the TE network
Land, no-objection certificates and utility diversions
Unit rates from recent NWS pre-investment appraisals, escalated to the tender date
STEP 1. CAPEX, phased across the construction years
STEP 4. Discount every flow to today at 5 percent over 25 years: NPV and life-cycle cost. Payback reported, but it does not decide
STEP 5. Repeat for three options per system, plus Option 0 do nothing
STEP 6. Score the seven criteria: lifetime cost, sustainability, in-country value, resilience, operability, constructability, environment
STEP 7. Apply the weights NWS sets
STEP 8. Test sensitivity on weighting, discount rate and design criteria. Within 10 percent on lifetime cost the greener option wins
Amber boxes are inherited from NWS pre-investment appraisal practice. Everything else follows PAM-GUD-201 sections 12.6 to 12.9
